commands.summary: 7 new tests fail without the change (env names, binding kinds, generated keys, runManifest, migration/app env)

notes: Cause: harness injected a fixed DB_*/CACHE_URL set from the capability registry and used binding names only. Production (compile.ts appEnvironment) injects DATABASE_URL/HOST/PORT/NAME/USER/PASSWORD, REDIS_URL/HOST/PORT, STORAGE_BUCKET/S3_BUCKET/AWS_S3_BUCKET, NODE_ENV, APP_API_KEY, APP_SIGNING_SECRET, then the manifest alias names by kind (incl. jdbc_url), then relay-minted deployz_generated keys (base64url 32).

Fix: buildAppEnvironment copies that rule; RunManifest carries binding {name, kind} and generatedKeys (new runManifest in local-run.ts); index.ts uses it; ctx.generateKey added; minted keys are redacted. Migration and app containers share the env.

Health path: harness already used the configured manifest (deploy-config overrides.healthPath wins over the manifest value), same as production; repo-556 probed /api/health and health PASSED. Its dbWrite FAIL came from the missing WAKAPI_DB_* alias names, fixed by the alias rule. No deploy-config change needed for repo-556.

Mapping: repo-529 APP_KEY via generatedKeys; 534 SPRING_DATASOURCE_* via kind aliases (jdbc_url); 543 DATABASE_* standard names; 551 app-specific URL alias names at migration; 556 WAKAPI_DB_* aliases. Not verified against real containers (no Docker run in this task); the rerun task must confirm.
Possible REPO_CONFIGURATION to check by rerun: repo-529 deploy-config has databaseRequired false while the app is a Laravel app that may need a database. Not edited.
Behavior change: DB_* and CACHE_URL are no longer injected unless the manifest binds them; NODE_ENV=production is now set as in production. Previous runs/ files unchanged; no product code touched.
